title: Cheat Sheet 1

lessons.title: Course Material: Cheat-Sheet (1).pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1 Write Your Expert Book –  Cheat Sheet  Introduction ü Everyone has a story to tell and many aspire to get it down on paper ü You might have even started writing your nonfiction book ü Self-publishing online is now a straightforward option to get your book out there ü Your concerns for writing could include: o You’re overwhelmed with ideas o You’re worried whether your writing is good enough o You don’t know how you’ll find the time o You don’t know if anyone will buy your book o You don’t know how to publish and market a book ü It is hard to write a book and requires dedication ü There’s a method to structure a book to take the pressure off ü Alleviate any concerns you might have ü A plan is vital to success ü Writing and publishing isn’t enough – people need to know about it ü You need to stand out from the crowd  What if there are already books in your specific area of expertise? ü Your book will be unique to you ü You’ll write in your own format and individual voice ü That’s what will set it apart

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2 The benefits of writing and publishing your book ü Use your knowledge to become recognized as an expert in your field ü Share your experience with a wide audience who need it ü Attract more people to your list and generate leads ü Generate revenue from book sales ü Open doors to better speaking arrangements ü Create related products based on your book content ü You get to share something you’re passionate about  ü Don’t underestimate the value of the sense of personal achievement ü You’ll be proud of what you’ve accomplished  Learning Objectives: ü Set goals for your book ü Write your book’s one-sentence defining statement ü Research your audience and choose your expert book topic ü Create a clear, logical outline for your book content ü List the expert content you already have to draw from ü Conduct any additional research you’ll need ü Plan your writing schedule and deadlines ü Prepare your book for publishing ü Build a profitable book sales funnel ü Create and implement a marketing plan  Action Steps: 1. Think about the benefits of writing your own book that are mentioned in this module.  2. Why do you want to write your book? What benefits will it bring to you and your readers?

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 Module 1 - Brainstorm Your Expert Book Idea  ü Set goals for your expert book, select a topic and write a description  Choose Your Goal(s) for Your Book ü Before you begin, set a goal for your book ü Get clarity on the purpose, and stay focused and motivated as you work through ü State a big long-term goal, then short-term smaller goals for your book to get you there ü This could look something like: o Ultimate goal:  § To become widely recognized as an expert in my field o Short term book goals: § Help boost credibility § Open doors to things like speaking engagements § Build an email list  ü These goals will also influence your choice of marketing tactics  Choose Your Book Topic ü You need to do some research into possible topics ü Narrow down results to find the best topic for you to write first

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 Step 1: Brainstorm ü Ask yourself the following questions: o What do you know a lot about? o What do you blog/speak/teach often? o What unique experiences do you have? o What knowledge do people know you for? o What referrals have you had? o For which skills are you constantly praised? o What do you feel most drawn to write about?  ü Write your ideas down ü Use bullet points, or a mind map ü If you have a lengthy selection, narrow it down ü Think about what problems your market faces ü What do you have to offer to solve those problems?  Step 2: Research ü Carry out market research on your list of possible topics ü Amazon o What books already exist? o Use keywords to do a search for popular examples o Is there a gap in the market? o Don’t be discouraged by something because it’s been covered before o Use reader reviews for inspiration o Is there potential for a series of books?

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 Find Out What Your Market Wants ü Carry out a survey on your blog, or in your Facebook group o Suggest some topics based on initial research o Ask people to suggest their own topics ü Engage people in a discussion o Email your list and ask them what their biggest problem is o Start a discussion on Facebook about possible topics o Ask them what they’re currently reading ü Your competitors o What books have your competitors published? o It’s ok to publish something similar o It will be unique with your knowledge, experience and perspective ü Quora o Search for what people are asking about your niche  o You’ll find inspiration for not only the topic, but the content   ü Keep a note of any subtopics or key content ideas you generate  Step 3: Choose Your Topic ü Create a shortlist of two or three topics ü Which will best show off your expertise and meet your goals? ü Which topic do you know the most about? ü Don’t get side-tracked by something too difficult ü Choose a topic that’s the combination of something you can write about and will showcase your expertise

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 Step 4: Define ü Write a one-sentence description of your book that says who it’s for ü This will give you a sense of direction ü Example: o My book helps ____ to _____ so that they can _____ .    Action Steps: 1. Write down your goals for your book. Write your big, overarching professional or business goal, and the goals for this specific book that will help you achieve that big goal. 2. Using the questions in Step 1 in this module, brainstorm ideas for your book.  3. Decide which methods of market research you will carry out and what you’ll look for. 4. Conduct your market research and record your results and notes in a separate notebook 5. Using your research results from Step 1 and Step 2 in this module, choose your topic for your book.  6. Write your defining statement for your book.

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 Module 2 - Writing Your Book  ü Creating an outline of your book is key to getting it done  ü Start creating your writing plan with goals and deadlines  Create Your Draft Book Outline ü A roadmap that takes you from the first sentence to finishing the book ü Keeps you focused and organized ü Makes sure you have a good flow  Step 1: Brainstorm Your Key Content ü The ideas you generate can be used for chapter titles, subtopics and key points ü Set a time limit and write as many ideas as you can ü Ignore your inner editor as all ideas are valid ü Frame your ideas as questions your readers might ask ü Record brainstorming  Step 2: Write Your Draft Outline Chapter titles ü Start by organizing and writing your chapter titles ü Give readers a clear idea of what to expect ü The main purpose now is to guide the logical flow of the content

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 Subtopics and Key Points ü Add the subtopics and key points you want to use from your brainstorming ü This is only a high-level outline ü Adds more explanation of the flow of the book  The Key Elements of a Non-Fiction Book ü Copyright page o Components such as your book title, subtitle and copyright statement ü Dedication o Add a dedication to someone special ü Acknowledgements o Acknowledge the help of the people who played a part in creating the book ü Table of Contents o List chapter titles and any subheadings ü Foreword o A short introduction written by someone other than the author ü Preface/Introduction o Include things like § Your background § Who the book is for  § What the reader can expect ü Chapters o The main body of your book content ü Bibliography o List any sources you’ve drawn from

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 ü About the Author o Your bio and any contact details you want to share  Create Your Writing Plan ü A detailed schedule of what you’re going to write and when ü Set goals and deadlines to stay on track o Set your deadline for completing research o Set your deadline for completing writing the main body o Set deadlines for completing each part of your book ü Make writing goals manageable  ü Write down tasks you need to complete in order of completion ü Schedule dates ü Work backwards from finish date ü Make writing a habit and a priority  Write every day ü Set aside a certain amount of time to write each day ü Set a goal of writing a certain amount of words a day ü The more you write the easier it gets  It’s Time to Write Your Book! Gather Content You Already Have and Organize it ü What relevant content can you repurpose? o Blog posts o Articles o Coaching content

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 o Podcasts o Video information o Webinars o Speech scripts o You’ll need to rewrite or reframe  Research Content Ideas ü Research will help expand your subtopics, key points and concepts ü Get info from print books, online content, or surveys ü Set a deadline for research so you don’t spend too long  Tools for Writing Your Book ü You can use a regular word processor such as Microsoft Word ü Try writing-specific software, such as Scrivener or Sigil ü Use OneNote or Evernote to capture research and ideas ü Use the Kindle Create Add-in to format  Tip ü Start writing main content first ü You’ll feel like you’re making progress quicker

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 Action Steps: Using the Outline & Planner: 1. Brainstorm content ideas for your book outline. Use the method you prefer to record your results – options include pen and paper, Word, and mind mapping software. 2. Using the ideas you generated in your brainstorming activities, create a draft outline of your book with your chapter titles, subtopics, and any key points.  3. Create your writing plan with goals and deadlines. Use your book outline as your guide and include a time limit and deadline for
